title: Association of Inflammatory Biomarkers and Ferritin With Severity of Pediatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Patients
off: Association of SII, NLR, PLR, and Ferritin With SLE Severity Pediatric Patients
summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn about the association of inflammatory biomarkers (SII, NLR, and PLR) and ferritin with disease severity in pediatric systemic lupus erythematosus (pSLE) patients. The main question it aims to answer is:

Are higher levels of SII, NLR, PLR, and ferritin associated with greater disease severity (mild, moderate, severe based on SLEDAI-2K score) in pediatric SLE patients?

Participants diagnosed with pediatric SLE will undergo routine blood tests to measure complete blood counts (NLR, PLR, SII) and serum ferritin, and their disease severity will be assessed using the SLEDAI-2K scoring system
desc:
Pediatric Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (pSLE) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by innate and adaptive immune activation, leading to autoantibody production, immune complex deposition, and systemic inflammation. Disease activity in pSLE is typically variable and fluctuating, requiring accurate and regular monitoring to optimize immunosuppressive therapy, prevent organ damage accumulation, and avoid treatment toxicity.

Although the Systemic Lupus Erythematosus Disease Activity Index 2000 (SLEDAI-2K) is widely established for assessing disease activity, its calculation relies on comprehensive clinical evaluations and specialized laboratory parameters (such as anti-dsDNA and complement levels) that may not be routinely available at every clinical encounter. Hematological indices derived from routine complete blood counts specifically the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII), Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR), and Platelet-to-Lymphocyte Ratio (PLR) along with serum ferritin (an acute phase reactant), reflect systemic inflammatory and immune dysregulation. These parameters represent low-cost, rapidly accessible, and widely available potential biomarkers for disease activity.

This observational study aims to evaluate the associations of SII, ferritin, NLR, and PLR with disease severity in pediatric SLE patients. Disease severity will be primarily categorized into mild, moderate, and severe stages based on the SLEDAI-2K score and analyzed as ordinal data, with secondary numerical SLEDAI-2K score analyses.

Because circulating blood cell counts and ferritin concentrations can also be influenced by non-SLE factors such as active infections, Macrophage Activation Syndrome (MAS), nutritional status, underlying hematological disorders, malignancies, and corticosteroid administration these clinical confounders will be rigorously evaluated and considered during statistical interpretation. The observed associations will be evaluated statistically to assess their potential clinical utility as supplementary markers for pSLE disease activity monitoring.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients aged 11-17 years.
* Diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus based on the 2012 SLICC/2019 EULAR/ACR criteria

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Patients with malignancies.
2. Patients with congenital abnormalities.
3. Patients who have experienced severe trauma or major surgery within four weeks prior to the examination.
4. Patients with liver disease or iron deficiency

arms.d: Pediatric patients diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus (pSLE). All participants undergo clinical and laboratory assessments, including complete blood counts to determine SII, NLR, and PLR, as well as serum ferritin levels. Disease severity is assessed and categorized into mild, moderate, or severe based on the SLEDAI-2K score

primary.tf: Baseline (at the time of evaluation / sample collection)
